Myth: Birth control pills cause infertility. 
This is one of the most common fertility misconceptions — and it stops women from making informed decisions about their reproductive health every single day.

The fact? There is no scientific evidence linking birth control pills to permanent infertility. Oral contraceptives temporarily suppress ovulation while you're on them. Once stopped, your natural cycle gradually resumes. For most women, fertility returns within a few months.

If you've been avoiding contraception out of fear or worrying about past pill use affecting your chances of conceiving  this is your clarity.

That said, if you've been trying to conceive for a while without success, the reason is unlikely to be your contraceptive history. Factors like age, PCOS, blocked fallopian tubes, low AMH, or male infertility are far more common causes worth investigating.

PELVIC FLOOR EXCERCISE-
Pelvic floor exercises (Kegels) strengthen the muscles that support your bladder and bowels. To locate the muscles, imagine stopping the flow of urine or trying to prevent passing gas. Squeeze and lift these muscles for 3-5 seconds, then relax completely for 3-5 seconds. Repeat 10-15 times per session, doing 3 sets daily.

How to do them right Follow these steps to ensure you are targeting the right muscles without straining:
Empty your bladder: Always start with an empty bladder to prevent discomfort.
Find the muscles: Squeeze the muscles that stop the flow of urine or hold back gas. You should feel a lifting sensation inside.
The Squeeze: Tighten these muscles and hold for 3 to 5 seconds.
The Relaxation: Relax completely for 3 to 5 seconds.
Set and Repetition: Repeat this 10 to 15 times in a row to complete one session.
Frequency: Do this 3 times a day (morning, afternoon, and 
night).

DYSMENORRHOEA
causes severe and frequent cramps and pain during your period. It may be either primary or secondary.

Primary dysmenorrhea. This occurs when you first start your period and continues throughout your life. It is usually life-long. It can cause severe and frequent menstrual cramping from severe and abnormal uterine contractions.

Secondary dysmenorrhea. This type is due to some physical cause. It usually starts later in life. It may be caused by another medical condition, such as pelvic inflammatory disease or endometriosis.

I truly don’t have enough words to express my gratitude for Dr Masrani & Dr Theertha.

Dr Masrani has become my go-to doctor for absolutely everything. I trust him with my life.
My journey with him began about five years ago when I consulted him for hormonal issues that were affecting my skin. From the very first interaction, his calm, reassuring, and unhurried way of explaining things put me completely at ease.

Over the years, he has guided me through multiple challenges. I underwent fibroid surgery under his care, and the entire experience was incredibly smooth. I was able to resume normal activity from Day 2. What stood out most was how clearly he explained the procedure beforehand, and post-surgery, he took the time to explain what had been resolved and what hadn’t giving me complete clarity and confidence.

One of the most critical moments for me was during a vacation when I experienced severe stomach pain that went undiagnosed. I reached out to Dr. Masrani, and he immediately advised a scan, which revealed a ruptured appendix. By the time I returned to Mumbai, everything was arranged overnight at Masrani Hospital, and the surgery was successfully performed. That level of responsiveness and care is something I will never forget.

Later, when my husband and I were trying to conceive, Dr. Masrani and Dr. Theertha supported us every step of the way. When I finally got pregnant, my entire pregnancy journey was incredibly positive and reassuring because of them. They were always available, patiently addressing every doubt and fear.
At the age of 36, I had a normal delivery, and what made it even more special was how empowered and fearless I felt throughout labour. I delivered within 8 hours of being admitted. Before discharge, the doctors even sat with us to prepare us for parenthood, what to expect as new parents and how to care for both the baby and me. That kind of holistic care is rare.

The support staff at the hospital are also incredibly kind, especially Nurse Harshali, who offered many useful tips on managing labour pain, caring for the baby, and overall recovery.

It is difficult to fully articulate how much my life has changed for the better through this journey. A huge part of that credit goes to Dr. Masrani and Dr. Theertha. I will forever be grateful.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I was admitted to Sapna Hospital for malaria and stayed for 4 days.
It was extremely concerning to see mosquito issues inside the ward while being treated for a mosquito-borne illness. A repellent machine was only provided after repeated complaints.
Hygiene standards were disappointing. I noticed what appeared to be blood stains in saline lines, a dustbin near my bed containing vomit that was not cleared promptly, and an ice pad provided to me that had visible hair on it. Used gloves were also left openly near patient beds instead of being disposed of immediately and bed bugs.
These are basic infection-control practices that should be strictly maintained in any hospital.
Staff behavior at times felt indifferent, and response seemed noticeably quicker when services involved billing.
For a bill of approximately ₹30,000 in just 3 days, I expected a much higher standard of cleanliness, monitoring, and patient care.
I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves hygiene control and patient handling to ensure patient safety.

We wanted a proper gap between our children. We were confused about the best way to go about it, but Ma’am sat us down and counseled us. She suggested the Copper T method and cleared all our myths about it.

For the last six years, she hasn't just been our "pregnancy doctor," she has been our family guide. Because of her planning and advice, we had a stress-free gap, and when we were finally ready again in 2026, everything went smoothly.

And guess what? Second baby, 2026—another normal delivery!

That is her specialty. She is so kind and such a good listener. You never feel like a "patient" with a file number; you feel like a person she genuinely cares about. She clears every doubt before you even leave the room. She gives you confidence when you are nervous and calm when you are stressed.

She doesn’t just deliver babies; she delivers peace of mind.

If you are looking for a doctor who supports natural birth and guides you through every stage of life, Dr. Prabhjot Manchanda is the one.

Thank you, Doctor!
